headline: Curve DEX core AMMs are autonomous: Stableswap and Cryptoswap pools have no external price oracles per Curve's own docs, pools are immutable post-deployment per audit, and any rate-oracle / underlying-asset exposure in NG pools is opt-in and isolated per-pool. Worst-case impacted TVS from any single external-dependency failure: <5% of total DEX TVL.
short_headline: Pools autonomous; isolated per-pool risk only

findings.text: Curve's own resources docs explicitly state: 'Curve Stableswap and Cryptoswap pools do not rely on external price oracles.' Cryptoswap pools price assets via an internal exponential-moving-average price_oracle computed from in-pool trade history; Stableswap pools use the StableSwap invariant on stored balances. The 3pool source (StableSwap3Pool.vy in curvefi/curve-contract) confirms no external oracle interface — only ERC20 token interfaces. The same docs explicitly warn that LLAMMA (which is part of crvUSD / Llamalend, separate DeFiLlama protocols, not curve-dex) does use external oracles — out of scope for this slice.

Stableswap-NG (curvefi/stableswap-ng) optionally supports per-pool rate oracles for rate-bearing tokens (wstETH, cbETH, sDAI, ERC4626 vaults). Per the repo README and the MixBytes audit, the rate-oracle address and method selector are packed into pool storage at deployment and read on each operation. These calls read the asset's OWN rate function (e.g. wstETH.stEthPerToken(), ERC4626.convertToAssets()) — they are intrinsic to the asset already in the pool, not a separate oracle service. Failure scope is limited to LPs in that specific pool who opted into that asset.

No off-chain oracle/reporter committee feeds into core Curve DEX pools. There is no exit-bus, no validator-set reporter, no price committee. Pricing in Stableswap/Cryptoswap pools is computed entirely on-chain from in-pool reserves and trade history.

Curve deploys independently on 29 chains (per pinned context). Each chain's pools are separate immutable contracts; pools do not share state across chains. The Q1-Q2 2025 progress report describes a Curve Block Oracle, deployed across 20+ chains, used for cross-chain DAO governance (propagating Ethereum mainnet block-hashes for storage proofs); it is a governance-control surface, not a pool-pricing dependency. CRV/crvUSD bridging exists for token economics but is not required for any pool to function. No material DEX TVL rides on a single non-canonical bridge as a load-bearing dependency for swap solvency.

Pool isolation: each Curve pool is its own contract holding only its declared asset set. Failure of an underlying asset (depeg, rebase exploit, rate-oracle manipulation for NG pools that use one) impacts only LPs of that specific pool, not the protocol as a whole. Per the autonomy guardrail, this is opt-in isolated-market risk that the user accepted at deposit time, not protocol-wide autonomy risk.
Curve is not a fork; original Stableswap design (2020 whitepaper, MixBytes/Quantstamp audits 2020). No forkedFrom lineage to record.

Mitigations against the per-pool risks identified: (i) LIVE — Cryptoswap and Stableswap-NG pools update their internal price_oracle at most once per block and use exponential moving averages, providing intra-block manipulation resistance for any pool used downstream as an oracle. (ii) LIVE — pool immutability (see A9) means a malicious upgrade cannot retroactively swap an external dependency in. (iii) LIVE — exchange_received in Stableswap-NG is intentionally disabled when rebasing tokens are present (per stableswap-ng repo README), preventing a known transfer-skim class of attack. No system-wide circuit breakers exist for AMM pools beyond the Emergency DAO's narrow kill-switch (control-slice scope).
Curve does NOT run its own L2 / appchain. Every deployment is permissionless on a third-party L1/L2; that chain's sequencer/consensus is substrate, not an A7 dependency per the slice scope rule.

AMM swaps and LP deposit/withdraw flows do not require keepers, relayers, or off-chain bots to maintain solvency or correctness. Pools function autonomously on user transactions. (Liquidation keepers are relevant to Llamalend / crvUSD, both separate protocols on DeFiLlama, not curve-dex.)

Existing Curve pools are immutable: per the MixBytes Stableswap-NG audit findings README ('pools' contracts do not allow upgrades, which means that users' tokens will get stuck on the contract'), and per the v1 curve-contract source style, the pool implementation is fixed at deployment with no upgrade slot. Governance (the DAO Voting Ownership Aragon app at 0xE478de... fetched on-chain at block 25038588 confirms supportRequiredPct=51%, minAcceptQuorumPct=30%, voteTime=604800 i.e. 1-week vote) can change documented parameters of existing pools (A coefficient, fees, ramp_A) but cannot swap the pool's coin set, oracle reference, or invariant logic. The pool factory can deploy NEW pools, but new pools do not affect existing pools' state. Therefore the autonomy-relevant criterion — 'can governance silently introduce a new external dependency into existing pools without an exit window' — is NO.

Caveat: legacy 'lending pools' from Curve v1 (e.g. Compound Pool, Y Pool, AAVE Pool) wrapped cTokens / aTokens / yTokens, with the underlying lent out on those external protocols. These pools DO have external dependencies on Compound/Aave/Yearn. They are largely deprecated (small TVS share today vs current Stableswap-NG, Tricrypto-NG, Twocrypto-NG pools) and are isolated per-pool. A user depositing into these pools opted into Compound/Aave risk; depositors in 3pool, Tricrypto, etc. are unaffected. Per A4, this is per-pool opt-in risk that does not propagate.

Sub-module enumeration and TVS weighting (rough — DeFiLlama TVS breakdown not separately fetched this run, see unknowns A-tvs): Module 1 = Stableswap v1 plain & metapools (3pool, FRAX/USDC, etc.) — no oracle, immutable, ~majority of historical TVS, grade green. Module 2 = Cryptoswap v1/v2 + Tricrypto + Tricrypto-NG — internal EMA only, immutable, meaningful share, grade green. Module 3 = Stableswap-NG — optional asset-intrinsic rate oracles, immutable, growing share (likely <30% of TVS), grade green per A1b/A4. Module 4 = Twocrypto-NG / Twocrypto — internal EMA only, smaller share, grade green. All four modules share the same autonomy properties (no protocol-wide external dependency, per-pool isolation, immutable pools); weighted overall = green because the worst-case unmitigated single-dependency failure is bounded at that one pool's TVS, and no module introduces a system-wide external oracle, bridge, keeper, or off-chain reporter.

steelman.red: Stableswap-NG pools that include rate-oracle tokens (wstETH, sDAI, cbETH) inherit the integrity of those rate functions, and legacy lending pools (cToken/aToken pools) deposit underlyings into Compound/Aave — a manipulation, exploit, or freeze of those external systems can directly impair LP principal in the affected pools, so Curve is not autonomy-clean.
steelman.orange: Although the core AMM math has no external dependencies and pools are immutable, the optional per-pool rate-oracle pattern in Stableswap-NG and the legacy lending-pool variants introduce external touchpoints whose failure can degrade or impair LPs in those specific pools, even though the impact is isolated rather than system-wide.
steelman.green: Curve's own documentation explicitly states Stableswap and Cryptoswap pools use no external price oracles; pools are immutable per audit (no upgrade path that could silently swap a dependency); rate-oracle and underlying-asset exposures in NG pools are per-pool, opt-in, and isolated, so a single external-dependency failure is bounded at that pool and cannot propagate to the rest of the DEX.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because the steel-man case for green is supported by Curve's own resource docs (Stableswap and Cryptoswap explicitly disclaim external price oracles), confirmed pool immutability from the MixBytes Stableswap-NG audit ('pools' contracts do not allow upgrades'), and per-pool isolation that matches the autonomy-slice guardrail carving out underlying-asset risk in opt-in isolated markets. The orange and red steel-mans rely on the rate-oracle pattern in Stableswap-NG and legacy lending pools, but both are precisely the per-market opt-in risk the rubric guardrail says does NOT make autonomy red on its own — a wstETH rate-oracle failure impacts only LPs of pools containing wstETH, not 3pool or Tricrypto LPs, and these pools collectively are a minority of TVS. No system-wide external dependency was identified across A1–A9: no oracle aggregator, no off-chain reporter committee feeding the AMMs, no bridge carrying material DEX TVL as a load-bearing dependency, no keeper liveness requirement for AMM solvency, and immutable pools that prevent governance from silently swapping a dependency in. Worst-case impacted TVS from any single external-dependency failure is <5% of total Curve DEX TVL, capped at the affected pool's individual TVL.

evidence.shows: Curve's official resources docs: 'Curve Stableswap and Cryptoswap pools do not rely on external price oracles.' Cryptoswap pools compute price_oracle internally as an EMA of last_prices. LLAMMA (out of scope: crvUSD/Llamalend) uses external price oracles — distinct module. Sourced for A1, A2, A6.

On-chain read at block 25038588: Curve DAO Voting (Ownership) Aragon app — supportRequiredPct=510000000000000000 (51%), minAcceptQuorumPct=300000000000000000 (30%), voteTime=604800 (7 days), votesLength=1404. Confirms governance is a 1-week token-weighted vote, not an EOA — relevant to A9 (governance can change parameters but only via vote, no instant dependency swap).

MixBytes audit of Curve Stableswap-NG. Explicit statement in a critical-severity finding: 'pools' contracts do not allow upgrades, which means that users' tokens will get stuck on the contract and there will be no possibility to retrieve them.' Confirms pool-level immutability post-deployment. Sourced for A9.

Curve Stableswap-NG repo README: 'Permissionless deployment of Curve Stableswap plain and metapools. Supports: rate-oraclised tokens (e.g. wstETH), ERC4626 (sDAI), rebasing (stETH), and plain (WETH:stETH) pools.' 'New pools are deployed via blueprints.' Confirms NG pools support optional per-pool rate oracles reading the asset's own rate function, deployed via immutable blueprint pattern. Sourced for A1b, A9.

Technical docs for Stableswap-NG: rate oracle in NG pools is configured per-pool, oracle precision must be 10^18, supports ERC20 with rate oracle (wstETH, cbETH, sDAI), ERC4626, and rebasing tokens. The pool reads stored_rates from the asset's own rate function. Confirms rate oracle is asset-intrinsic, not a separate price service. Sourced for A1b.

Cryptoswap technical overview: 'Curve v2 pools automatically adjust liquidity to optimize depth close to the prevailing market rates... by tracking a continuous EMA (exponential moving average) of the pool's latest exchange rates (referred to as an internal oracle).' Confirms Cryptoswap uses an internal EMA, no external oracle. Sourced for A1.

Source code of the canonical Curve 3pool (StableSwap3Pool.vy): only imports ERC20 and a CurveToken interface for the LP token; no oracle interface or external price feed; pool prices via the StableSwap invariant on stored balances of DAI/USDC/USDT. Confirms v1 plain pools have zero external-pricing dependencies. Sourced for A1.

DeFiLlama page for Curve Finance lists three distinct sub-protocols: 'Curve DEX', 'crvUSD', and 'Curve LlamaLend', each with separate fee/revenue accounting. Confirms that the curve-dex slug is scoped to the AMM pools only, with crvUSD and LlamaLend (which use LLAMMA + external oracles) treated as separate protocols. Sourced for the scope boundary used throughout.

Curve quarterly progress report (March-May 2025): 'Curve Block Oracle... now enables secure cross-chain governance and DAO controlled deployments on other networks... deployed across more than 20 chains where Curve smart contracts have been deployed, supporting secure cross-chain messaging and distribution of Ethereum mainnet b[lockhashes]'. Confirms cross-chain Block Oracle is governance infrastructure (DAO control propagation), not a pool pricing dependency. Sourced for A3.

Curve audit registry listing audits by MixBytes (22 Jul 2020 Curve DAO; 27 Sep 2021 Stableswap-NG; 5 Jun 2023 Curve Stablecoin), Quantstamp (5 Aug 2020 Curve DAO Contracts; 15 Oct 2020 Metapools), ChainSecurity (27 Sep 2021 ETH/sETH; 29 Sep 2021 Tricrypto; 23 Jun 2023 Tricrypto-NG; 1 Apr 2022 Twocrypto; 25 Sep 2024 FeeSplitter; 24 Jan 2024 and 12 Dec 2023 Curve Stablecoin), StateMind (2 Feb 2024). Sourced for protocol_metadata.audits.

Curve metaregistry README enumerates the active pool factory/registry surface: 'Curve Stable Factory: A permissionless StableSwap pool factory... Curve Crypto Registry: A registry of custom CryptoSwap pool implementations... Curve Crypto Factory: A permissionless CryptoSwap pool factory.' Confirms the four sub-module classes (Stableswap, Cryptoswap, plus NG variants from stableswap-ng) covered in A-modules.

unknowns: A-tvs: precise per-module TVS shares (Stableswap v1 vs Cryptoswap vs Stableswap-NG vs Twocrypto-NG / Tricrypto-NG) were not fetched from DeFiLlama in this run — verdict relied on architectural-equivalence reasoning (all modules share the same autonomy properties: no protocol-wide external oracle, per-pool isolation, immutable pools), so weighted grade = green regardless of exact splits. A future run should fetch DeFiLlama breakdown to confirm.

A1b-offchain: I could not enumerate every Stableswap-NG pool on Ethereum or other chains and read each one's rate-oracle configuration on-chain (no pool addresses were in the pinned address_book; defipunkd surfacers for non-pinned addresses are blocked by the allowlist). Per the slice's unknown rubric (multi-market protocol where per-market enumeration is infeasible), this gap does NOT block grading the architecture, but a future run should add representative NG pool addresses (e.g. wstETH/ETH-NG, sDAI-3pool-NG, USDe-NG) to the address book for direct on-chain rate-oracle verification.

A3-offchain: cross-chain CRV / crvUSD canonical bridge addresses were not surfaced this run (none in address_book). Curve's cross-chain page exists at resources.curve.finance/cross-chain/ but was not directly fetched. Future runs should pin the Curve cross-chain bridge endpoints to verify the trust model carries no material DEX TVL.

A1-legacy: precise current TVS share of legacy lending pools (Compound, Y, AAVE, BUSD, etc.) was not fetched this run; cited as 'small/legacy' from architectural context. A future run should query the metaregistry for these legacy pool addresses and check current balances.

protocol_metadata.about: Curve DEX is an automated market maker (AMM) for stablecoin and pegged-asset swaps on Ethereum and 28 other chains, where users swap tokens or provide liquidity to earn trading fees and CRV emissions. Stableswap pools (3pool, FRAX/USDC, etc.) use a hybrid constant-sum/constant-product invariant for low-slippage stablecoin trades; Cryptoswap and Tricrypto pools use a dynamic-peg invariant with internal EMA price tracking for volatile-asset pairs; Stableswap-NG adds optional per-pool rate oracles for rate-bearing tokens (wstETH, sDAI, cbETH) and dynamic fees. Pools are immutable and deployed permissionlessly via blueprint factories. Note: the Curve Finance umbrella also includes crvUSD (the LLAMMA-based stablecoin) and Curve Llamalend (lending markets) — these are separate DeFiLlama protocols with their own external-oracle dependencies and are not in scope for this curve-dex assessment.
